Headteacher's Welcome
We warmly welcome all children and families to our vibrant Catholic school community. Here at Our Lady Immaculate, we celebrate the unique gifts and talents of each child, fostering a love of learning and a strong foundation in faith.Our curriculum is enriched by the Catholic tradition, nurturing the spiritual growth of all students. We embrace diversity and inclusion, creating a welcoming environment where everyone feels valued and respected.We invite you to explore our website and learn more about our approach to education. We look forward to partnering with you on your child's educational journey.
Our Vision Statement
In our community we aim to:
Thrive together as God's children on our spiritual journey.
Develop our partnership with children, parents, parish, teachers and wider community.
Love and respect one another, valuing diversity and differences.
Encourage the development of a growth mind-set, build resilience and positive wellbeing.
Provide enriching learning experiences, which foster a lifelong love of learning.
"At OLI, we ignite a love of learning with an ambitious and enriching curriculum. All children explore every subject outlined in the National Curriculum, taught creatively to foster both knowledge and essential skills. This focus on well-rounded development empowers them to build a strong understanding across all subjects. As a result, our children are not only prepared for success beyond OLI, but also equipped to be well-informed and engaged global citizens."

Our Catholic Mission
At Our Lady Immaculate, Religious Education is more than just an academic subject; it is the cornerstone of the entire educational experience.
The objective is to integrate Catholic beliefs and traditions into every aspect of school life, creating an environment where faith is both taught and lived.
Our school mission statement is lived out in many ways.
Integration of Faith and Education
Holistic Faith Experience
Role Models and Personal Example
Faith in Action
By integrating the principles above into both the curriculum and the daily life of the school, our Catholic education aims to nurture well-rounded individuals who are prepared to live out their faith in every aspect of their lives.

Curriculum Vision
We provide an ambitious and challenging curriculum for all children at OLI. Every child experiences all of the subjects on the National Curriculum and these are taught creatively with a focus on knowledge and skills. We believe that, through this focus, the children can forge a strong understanding across all areas of the curriculum. This understanding allows all children to reach their potential at OLI and beyond as global citizens.
Through a progressive and engaging curriculum, we provide our children with opportunities to...
Our goal is to prepare each child to confidently embrace their future as active, considerate, and loving members of society.

Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education, we aim to actively promote British values in school to ensure our pupils leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
You can view our British Values Statement here to see how these values are embedded in life at OLI.

Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching (CST) is based on the belief that God has a plan for creation, a plan to build his kingdom of peace, love and justice. It holds that God has a special place in this story for each of us, whoever we are. Our part in this plan isn’t just limited to things ‘spiritual’, or things we might do on Sundays, but that it involves every aspect of our lives, from the things we pray about, to how we live as responsible global citizens. Our part in this story is a vocation for the common good, a call to treat everyone as your brothers and sisters and is something that we all share.
The 7 main principles of CST are:
Dignity
Solidarity
The Common Good
The Option for the Poor
Peace
Care for Creation
The Dignity of Work And Participation
Read more about some of the CST principles at https://cafod.org.uk/Pray/Catholic-social-teaching

pageCache.text:
Faith Education for All
The outcome of excellent religious education is religiously literate and consciously engaged young people who have the knowledge, understanding, and skills – appropriate to their age and capacity – to reflect spiritually, and think ethically and theologically, and who recognise the demands of religious commitment in everyday life.
The Religious Education Directory for Catholic Schools.
Catholic schools have a unique opportunity to promote interfaith dialogue and understanding while maintaining their Catholic identity and principles. Here at our Lady Immaculate, we aim to effectively engage with and respect the diverse religious backgrounds of pupils and staff by creating an inclusive environment
We ensure that all pupils and staff feel respected and valued, regardless of their religious background. This is reflected in the school's policies, practices, and the respectful language used by everyone in the school community. We are aware of and are sensitive to the various religious practices and needs of students, such as dietary restrictions, dress codes, and prayer requirements.
Within our curriculum, we include education about various world religions. Pupils are taught about the beliefs, practices, and significant festivals of the different religions - especially those reflected in our school cohort, such as Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Orthodox Christianity.
We strive to ensure the high quality of learning about other World Religions by inviting members of different faith communities to speak about their beliefs and practices. This provides students with firsthand insight and fosters a greater understanding and respect for other religions.
By integrating these strategies, Catholic schools can create a rich, inclusive environment that honours and respects religious diversity while staying true to their Catholic identity. This approach not only enriches the educational experience but also prepares students to live in a multicultural and multi-faith world.
Our Religious Education - Subject on a Page summarises our intent, implementation and desired impact for this core subject at Our Lady Immaculate.

Service & Charity
At OLI, we are deeply committed to supporting local charities and fostering a spirit of service among our students.
Each year, we participate in fundraising initiatives for the OLI Parish Lenten project, uniting our efforts to make a meaningful impact. Our students bring joy to the local community in a number of ways such as singing carols during the Christmas season, spreading holiday cheer. Additionally, we organise food collection drives to support local food banks, ensuring that those in need receive essential supplies. We also host events to raise funds for the Catholic Children's Society Crisis Fund, demonstrating our dedication to helping vulnerable children and families in times of crisis.

pageCache.text:
Wellbeing Ambassadors
- Listening, Supporting and Sharing Strategies -
Our Wellbeing Ambassadors are pupils who have shown a real interest in championing positive mental health and wellbeing. They have a responsibility to lead and promote wellbeing throughout school. They offer vital peer-to-peer support for our pupils, promoting conversations about how to be mentally healthy and signposting adult support for those who need it. Children benefit from developing more positive relationships, an increased sense of belonging in their school or setting, increased confidence and resilience and improved wellbeing. The Wellbeing Ambassadors working towards this together by...
Attending training to develop their discussion and listening skills.
Learning how and when to signpost others to help available.
Assisting with wellbeing assemblies.
Attending Mental Health conferences.
On Thursday 9th November, five of our Year 6 Wellbeing Ambassadors attended the Primary Mental Health Conference held at Southborough High School. Alongside many other primary children from around the borough, they participated in activities designed to stimulate discussions around mental health and learned about ways in which we can help ourselves and others when we are struggling. Finally, they created an action plan for the Wellbeing Ambassadors at OLI which included training, leading an assembly, helping organise our Wellbeing Week and creating a noticeboard to spotlight our activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Lady Immaculate Catholic Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
At Our Lady Immaculate School the Music curriculum is designed to develop a love and appreciation for Music in all pupils.
All children will have the opportunity to engage in the key areas of learning: listening; singing; composing and performing through a range of different learning activities reflecting the world they live in now, giving them access to musical styles throughout history and exploring how they can contribute to music in the future. All children will have equal opportunities to have hands-on experiences, interacting with various pitched and unpitched musical instruments.
Starting in Reception and Year 1 playing percussion instruments, the children then build on this through learning handbells in Year 2, recorders in Year 3, ukulele in Year 4, Djembe drums in Year 5 and keyboards in Year 6.
We aim that our children continue to grow in confidence as they progress through the musical curriculum and develop a lifelong appreciation of music.
